findings.summary: install.sh now exists but the stable channel 404s on releases/latest/download/latest.json; --edge works.
findings.evidence: curl -fsSL https://cp-lang.org/install.sh | sh -> 'cpl-install: error: could not download https://github.com/ryanbai1412/cp-lang/releases/latest/download/latest.json'; `sh -s -- --edge` installs edge-2026-11-23-528cddc4

findings.summary: Pasting now keeps indentation, but typing Enter after a ':' header does not indent; it only copies the previous line's indent, so typed blocks come out flat or double-indented.
findings.evidence: https://cp-lang.org/play/ type 'for x in a:<Enter>if x > 10:<Enter>print(x)' -> error[E0104]: expected an indented block after the `for` header

findings.summary: An indentation error also produces a cascading 'no `x` in scope' error for the loop variable, two errors for one root cause.
findings.evidence: play: 'for x in a:\nif x > 10:\nprint(x)' -> E0104 at line 6 plus 'error[E0201]: no `x` in scope --> line 6'

findings.summary: Guides mix `none` (tour) and `None` (cheat sheet, practice), and `@memo` vs `@cache`; release notes say 0.3 renamed them but the compiler is 0.2.2, so it's unclear which spelling compiles.
findings.evidence: /docs/guides/tour 'var best: ?Int = none' vs /docs/guides/cheatsheet 'var best: ?Int = None'; /docs/releases '0.3.0 (unreleased) ... @cache instead of @memo'

findings.summary: Range-sums practice reference solution still builds the prefix table by hand; Prefix(a).fold(l..=r) works but the docs offer 4 spellings (prefix(a), Prefix(a), a.scan(+), Prefix(+, a)).
findings.evidence: https://cp-lang.org/learn/practice/range-sums/ reference: 'var pre: [V.cuts]Int = 0; for v in V: pre[v.r] = pre[v.l] + a[v]'; mine 'let pre = Prefix(a); print(pre.fold(l..=r))' accepted 4/4

findings.summary: Run-length practice teaches a manual two-pointer while loop although the stdlib documents a.runs().
findings.evidence: https://cp-lang.org/learn/practice/run-length/ reference uses 'while j < s.len and s[j] == s[i]: j += 1'; /docs/guides/stdlib lists 'a.runs()'

findings.summary: The Neovim (and Helix) setup on /setup is `vim.opt.rtp:append('/path/to/cp-lang/editors/neovim')`, i.e. it needs a repo checkout, which the installer does not ship; I configured Neovim's built-in vim.lsp with `cpl lsp` myself instead.
findings.evidence: https://cp-lang.org/setup/ step 2, Neovim tab; ls ~/.cpl/toolchains/*/ has no editors/ dir. Workaround init.lua: vim.filetype.add({extension={cp='cpl'}}); vim.lsp.config('cpl',{cmd={'cpl','lsp'},filetypes={'cpl'}}); vim.lsp.enable('cpl')

findings.summary: VS Code has no published extension (.vsix, Marketplace and Open VSX all 'not published yet'); the only path is `cd editors/vscode && npm install && npm run package` from a repo checkout, which the rules forbid, so VS Code has no CPL support.
findings.evidence: https://cp-lang.org/setup/ VS Code tab; curl 'https://open-vsx.org/api/-/search?query=cp-lang' and the VS Marketplace extensionquery for 'cp-lang' return no CP Lang extension

findings.summary: JetBrains Marketplace install is 'not published yet'; the plugin must be built from editors/jetbrains with ./gradlew buildPlugin in a repo checkout, so IntelliJ/CLion get no CPL support.
findings.evidence: https://cp-lang.org/setup/ JetBrains tab; curl 'https://plugins.jetbrains.com/api/searchPlugins?search=cp%20lang' -> {"plugins":[],"total":0}

findings.summary: The site has no plain-Vim (no-LSP-client) instructions; I wired `makeprg=cpl check %` with a hand-written errorformat and `equalprg=cpl fmt --stdin`, and borrowed Python syntax for highlighting.
findings.evidence: https://cp-lang.org/setup/ has tabs VS Code/Neovim/Helix/Zed/Emacs/JetBrains only; ~/.vimrc: au BufRead,BufNewFile *.cp setlocal ft=python makeprg=cpl\ check\ % errorformat=%Eerror[%.%#]:\ %m,%Z\ \ -->\ %f:%l:%c,%-G%.%# equalprg=cpl\ fmt\ --stdin

findings.summary: `cpl fetch <codeforces url>` gets a 403 from Codeforces; I had to save each page from the browser (scripted over CDP) and pass --html.
findings.evidence: cpl fetch https://codeforces.com/contest/2285/problem/A cf2285A -> 'cpl: could not download ...: curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 403; save the page from the browser and pass it with `--html page.html`'

findings.summary: The fetched skeleton is `let n: 1..=2e5 = read()` with no `@!multitest` although every one of the 10 statements says 'Each test contains multiple test cases'; every file needed the header added by hand.
findings.evidence: cpl fetch https://codeforces.com/contest/2285/problem/A cf2285A --html 2285A.html; cat cf2285A.cp -> '// limits: 1000 ms, 256 MB\n\nlet n: 1..=2e5 = read()'

findings.summary: cf2285A accepts any valid permutation but `cpl test` compares tokens against the sample answer and fails; I wrote a Python checker and passed it with --checker (a file-local `@check` is documented for stress, not for `cpl test`).
findings.evidence: cpl test cf2285A -> 'first difference at line 2, token 2: expected `3`, got `2` / 0/1 passed'; cpl test cf2285A --checker 'python3 chk2285A.py' -> 2/2 passed

findings.summary: The method `a.inversions()` documented in the seq reference is still E0203 on arrays and lists, but the free function `use std.seq.{inversions}; inversions(s)` now works (run 1: not implemented at all).
findings.evidence: print([3,1,2].inversions()) -> 'error[E0203]: a `List<Int>` has no method `inversions` that `cpl run` knows'; 'use std.seq.{inversions}\nprint(inversions([3,1,2]))' -> 2

findings.summary: I wanted the prefix sums S1..Sn as a sequence for the min check and inversion count; `a.scan(+)` gives a `Prefix<D, Int>` without .inversions, so I wrote the running-sum loop by hand.
findings.evidence: cf2289D: 'let s = a.scan(+); print(inversions(s))' -> 'error[E0203]: a `Prefix<D, Int>` has no method `inversions`'; replaced by 'var s: [0..n]Int = 0; var run = 0; for i in 0..n: run += a[i]; s[i] = run'

findings.summary: Stress derived a non-permutation (`1 1`) for `let p: [V]V = read()` so my brute and fast disagreed on invalid input; `Perm<V>` fixes it but needs `use std.seq.{Perm}` (a type in the input declaration not in the prelude).
findings.evidence: cf2289C with 'let p: [V]V = read()' -> cpl stress saves stress-1.in '1\n2\n1 1'; 'let p: Perm<V> = read()' -> help: `Perm` is in the standard library: add `use std.seq.{Perm}`

findings.summary: `var c = b` on a List moves it (E-borrow 'moved here'), so a BFS brute needed `b.clone()`; fine once known but surprising coming from C++ value copies.
findings.evidence: for b in frontier: for i in 1..n: var c = b; c[i] = -b[i] -> 'moved here ... help: use `b.clone()` where it was moved if you still need `b`'

findings.summary: Under `@!multitest`, a `@gen` must print the test count itself (derived generators add it automatically); the docs' @gen examples are all single-test, so my first gens fed `2 2\n10` to the brute and it died with Code(3).
findings.evidence: cf2285B with '@gen fn make_case(size: Int): print(n, rand(0, n)); print(s)' -> 'error: the brute cf2285B.cp (`slow`) failed on this input (Code(3)), so there is nothing to compare with: 2 2 / 10'; adding print(1) fixes it

findings.summary: For a read-n-then-q-queries problem (cf2285D) an `@alt(program)` cannot use the input at all: every top-level name is 'the solution's own work' because the last read() is inside the query loop, so I gave up stressing D and kept hand tests.
findings.evidence: cf2285D + '@alt(program) fn slow(): for _ in 0..q: let (i, v) = read() ...' -> 'error[E0201]: `q` is the solution's own work: a brute or a checker shares only the input / help: it sees every top-level line down to the last `read()`; compute the rest inside the fn' (also for `n`, `a`)

findings.summary: The off-by-one counterexample was reported as 'shrunk from 9 numbers to 9' (n=6) although n=2 `2 1` style cases also fail, so shrinking did nothing for a @gen-based case.
findings.evidence: bug/b_bug.cp (cf2289B with run_end '... else: i + 1'); cpl stress b_bug.cp -> 'FAIL on case 11 (seed 11): WA / shrunk from 9 numbers to 9: 1 / 6 5 / 2 1 1 1 1 1'

findings.summary: cf2289A wants Yes/No; the docs say yes(b) prints YES/NO and point to `if ok: "Yes" else: "No"`, which I used so `cpl test` matches the sample exactly (test-exact-case-yes-no not re-tested).
findings.evidence: /docs/guides/io-and-formatting: 'print(yes(ok)) // YES or NO (for AtCoder Yes/No, use print(if ok: "Yes" else: "No"))'

findings.summary: `xs.shuffled()` is answered with 'help: did you mean `shuffle`?', but `xs.shuffle()` then fails with E0203 too; the working spelling is the prelude free function `shuffle(mut xs)` (the method form is in the IndexedMut table).
findings.evidence: 'var all = [c for c in 0..=8]; all.shuffle()' -> 'error[E0203]: a `List<Int>` has no method `shuffle` that `cpl run` knows'; '[..].shuffled()' -> 'help: did you mean `shuffle`?'; 'shuffle(mut all)' works

findings.summary: With a g++ binary `cf2272A` next to `cf2272A.cp`, `cpl test cf2272A` tries to read the binary as source and fails, so binaries need their own folder.
findings.evidence: g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -o cf2272A cf2272A.cpp; cpl test cf2272A -> 'cpl: can't read cf2272A: stream did not contain valid UTF-8'

findings.summary: Writing rows[1] while `let r = rows[0]` is alive is rejected (as predicted), but the reason says '(one contains the other)', which is wrong for two sibling elements; it is the whole-`rows` lend that conflicts.
findings.evidence:
design/p4.cp: 'var rows = [[1, 2], [3]]
let r = rows[0]
rows[1].push(5)
print(r.len)' -> 'error[E0602]: `rows[1]` can't be changed here: `rows` is lent to `r` until its last use (one contains the other)'

findings.summary: Still as in run 1: `a.rev[0]` is `a[0]` (identity keys), not the last element; the identity-vs-offset chapter explains why, but C++ habit expects `rbegin()[0]`.
findings.evidence: 'let a = [5, 1, 4]; let r = a.rev; print(r[0])' -> 5

findings.summary: Still as in run 1: `.count()` on a list of Bools returns the length (3), not the number of trues (2); you need `.count(x => x)`.
findings.evidence: 'print([true, false, true].count())' -> 3

findings.summary: Still as in run 1: `(0..3).argmax(i => a[i])` gives a `for`-walk error about `Items<Range<Int>>` instead of naming the missing argmax-with-key spelling.
findings.evidence: 'let a = [5, 1, 4]; print((0..3).argmax(i => a[i]))' -> 'error[E0302]: a `for` can't walk over a `Items<Range<Int>>`'; a.argmax() -> 0 works

findings.summary: Still as in run 1: the docs show both `let xs = compress(all)` (domain `xs.D`) and `let (domain C, comp) = compress(xs)`.
